title: Why total silence makes your ears ring
caption:
Silence isn't empty — it's why your ears ring.
A cartoon guy hops into bed savoring the quiet, then jolts upright clutching his ears as a phantom whistle screams through the totally silent bedroom.
In total silence your brain turns up its auditory gain, amplifying background nerve activity until you 'hear' a ring — and a fan's white noise masks it.
Do you fall asleep with a fan or white noise on, or can you handle total silence?
Save this for tonight and follow for more everyday body science.
